measured_reference.paper: Jacobson et al. (2008), Revised Orbits of Saturn's Small Inner Satellites, AJ 135, 261–263, Table 2
measured_reference.retrieval_note: Publisher abstract and indexed text of primary-paper Table 2 were accessible; direct publisher/PDF fetches failed. Numerical e/i are independently consistent with Torii Table 1.
measured_reference.reference: Saturn equatorial planetocentric; longitudes from Saturn-equator/ICRF-equator node; precessing mean elements, not native spherical Kepler osculating elements.

current_jpl.warning: JPL warns that mean elements must not be used to compute ephemerides; current rounded Daphnis entries e=0.000 and i=0.0 do not resolve these small values.

primary_context.relevant: Torii et al. Table 1 reproduces early-Cassini e/i estimates; later orbital variation is discussed. Their results separate large-scale inclined-orbit bending from localized collision-induced walls.

observation_2009.note: Photometric phase is not moon argument of latitude, true anomaly or node. Caption does not provide exact exposure time or orbital phase.

phase_limit: No 2006/2009 observed orbital phase is assigned. A specific exposure UTC, a consistent ephemeris and equatorial-frame transform are required. Published epoch angles do exist, but extrapolating a spherical Kepler orbit from them does not reproduce precessing Saturn-system ephemerides. All experiment f/u angles are declared sensitivity choices.
